title: Golden Shift Detector: CI perf gates for kernel routing, attention optimizations, and prefill/decode schedules
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: Build a continuous golden-shift detector and CI perf gating layer that automatically identifies performance regressions tied to kernel selection decisions, attention micro-optimizations, and prefill/decode scheduling changes. The detector will maintain per-workload golden baselines, compute drift metrics, and triage anomalous runs into actionable alerts and automated CI failures when regressions exceed configured thresholds.

Background: We frequently run into subtle regressions after kernel routing or attention changes that only appear on a subset of workloads (e.g., long-prefix conversations or attention-windowed models). Current bench runs produce telemetry but lack an automated, workload-aware comparator to decide when to block merges. This ticket implements a detection+gating mechanism integrated with our benchmark harness and CI.

Goals:
- Create a golden baseline store for canonical workload cohorts (short/med/long prefill, chat-like, instruction-following, decode-heavy).
- Compute per-run drift scores for latency P50/P90/P99, memory peak, and throughput delta and attribute them to kernel routing or scheduler flags where possible.
- Add gating rules in CI that fail PRs when a statistically significant regression is detected for at least one golden cohort beyond thresholds.
- Provide triage page linking failing runs to candidate commits, kernel selection matrices, and prefills/decoder profiles.
- Keep false positives under control through rolling baselines, confidence windows, and optional test-blacklisting.

Deliverables:
1) Golden baseline catalog (versioned artifacts) with metadata: workload-id, seed-corpus hash, kernel-routing matrix, attention-mode flags, sequence-length distribution.
2) Drift scoring library (python) used by bench harness to emit a single drift report JSON per run.
3) CI gate plugin that consumes drift report and matches against rules (thresholds configurable per workload).
4) Triage dashboard in Console (bench-triage) with links to relevant PRs, perf traces, and kernel heatmaps.
5) Runbook for on-call and release engineers describing remediation steps and fallback policies.

Approach & Implementation Notes:
- Workload cohorts will be drawn from our canonical corpus and seeded with deterministic RNG for repeatability. We'll store golden artifacts in s3://redwood-bench/gold/v1 with checksums.
- Drift metrics: use non-parametric effect sizes (e.g., Hodges-Lehmann) and bootstrap to avoid normality assumptions. For latency, report relative delta and absolute ms at P50/P90/P99. For memory/peak, use absolute MB delta. For throughput, tokens/s percent change.
- Attribution heuristics: correlate drift spikes with kernel-routing matrices (which kernels executed for each op) and prefill/decoder scheduling flags; compute a heatmap of co-occurrence and surface top-3 suspects.
- CI gating: default thresholds P90 latency > +10% and +25ms OR P99 > +20% and +50ms triggers a soft-fail (report + block checkbox). For high-priority routes (customer-facing hosted api), thresholds are stricter and will auto-fail. Gates will be configurable via .bench-config in repo or global defaults.
- Stability controls: implement hysteresis (require regression persist across N runs within T hours) and a rolling baseline update mechanism (golden updates require manual approval).

Testing Plan:
- Unit tests for drift library, synthetic regression injection tests (we will create noise-injection harness that alters kernel selection probabilities and ensures detector flags regressions).
- End-to-end bench job that runs against runtime canary and compares to gold; test both detection and CI plugin behavior.
- Run on a sample of historical PRs (replay) to validate lack of excessive false positives.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Golden catalog exists for the 6 initial cohorts and is versioned in S3.
- Drift library has >= 90% unit test coverage and CI plugin can read drift reports and produce pass/fail signals.
- At least two known historical regressions (identified from past incidents) are reproducibly detected by the new detector in replay mode.
- Triage dashboard shows kernel-level attribution for flagged runs and links to PRs/bench artifacts.
- Runbook published in Confluence with remediation steps and escalation path.

Observability & Dashboards:
- Bench-triage dashboard: per-cohort P50/P90/P99 time series, drift-score histogram, top-kernel-suspects.
- CI gate dashboard: PR-level pass/fail history and false-positive rate.
- Telemetry exported to data warehouse for long-term analysis.

Links & Artifacts: 
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/DEVENG/Golden+Shift+Detector (draft)
- Design notes and kernel-heatmap prototype: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1KernelHeatmapPrototype
- Draft bench harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench/pull/4382 (WIP)
- Experimental triage dashboard (read-only): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/bench-triage-experiment

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: spurious CI failures slow merges. Mitigation: soft-fail path and human-in-loop approval, plus conservative thresholds initially.
- Risk: attribution noisy for concurrent changes (kernel + scheduler + quantization). Mitigation: require additional targeted microbench runs that isolate variable changes when flagging a suspected kernel.

Open Questions: 
- Policy for baseline updates: who approves gold bump? Suggest: PM + two eng approvers.
- Storage retention: how many gold versions to keep? Recommend keep last 6 months by default.

Next steps:
- Week 1: finalize cohort definitions, create initial gold artifacts for 6 cohorts (ENG-12910 owns artifact creation).
- Week 2: implement drift library and hook into bench harness; run replay tests.
- Week 3: integrate CI plugin and wire up triage dashboard; run on canary PRs and tune thresholds.

Owners: Marco Reyes (owner for CI integration), Priya Nair (owner for dashboard/triage), Aisha Khan (owner for cohort definitions and runbook).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Golden catalog present and versioned for 6 cohorts in s3; 2) Drift library produces reproducible drift reports; 3) CI plugin enforces gates for configured cohorts; 4) Triage dashboard displays attribution heatmaps and links to PR/bench artifacts; 5) Runbook documented in Confluence.

notes: This ticket intentionally aims to reduce manual triage load and provide deterministic blocking signals for perf regressions. It will evolve to cover quantization and new kernel backends in subsequent phases.
estimated_cost: ~12 GPU-hours per full golden replay run
